Steam Machine priced at $1,049, Valve officially confirms

en.commentary:
The advice I gave for fifteen years, that you should build your own machine to save money, expired this year. A 32GB DDR5-6000 kit that sold for roughly $80 in mid-2025 is asking about $432 today, July alone added another 7% to DDR5 contract pricing, and the market now sits 448% above where it was twelve months ago. The big system builders bought memory and NAND by the container before the spike and locked those costs in, so a boxed machine in August 2026 frequently lands under the cart of parts that would recreate it. I have priced that comparison four times this month and the prebuilt won every time.

That makes the Valve Steam Machine the most useful object in this entire category. Valve states plainly that it sells the box at cost, which turns the $1,049 sticker into a public receipt for what June 2026 silicon really costs. Roughly six times Steam Deck graphics performance for that money is the line every other machine here has to clear. It lands at second because SteamOS runs about 25,000 games and your library probably includes titles outside that set, and because Valve is still working through a reservation queue it expects to clear by year end.

The Lenovo Legion Tower 7i Gen 10 takes the top spot at $1,709 for an RTX 5070 Ti, a Core Ultra 7 265F, 32GB of DDR5 and a 1200W supply. Divide the frame rate by that price and it wins outright, and the internals are a standard ATX board with a standard 24-pin connector, so the machine stays alive through two more GPU generations.

One habit will save you more money than any brand choice: order the base memory configuration and buy your own sticks. The factory 16GB to 32GB upgrade currently runs between $120 and $360 depending on the brand, for the same commodity DIMMs.

highlights.title: The Steam Machine is the ruler every other box gets measured with
highlights.body: Valve confirmed it sells the Steam Machine at cost, $1,049 for the 512GB model and $1,349 for the 2TB version, and said the original target was closer to $750 before memory and NAND pricing moved. That makes it the only machine in this category with a published, honest bill of materials attached to it. I use it as a baseline: any Windows tower asking more than $1,049 needs to show clearly more performance for the difference. That single test replaces an afternoon of spec-sheet reading, and it is the reason a $2,399 machine with an RTX 5070 scores where it does on cost per frame.

highlights.title: Lenovo wins because $1,709 buys an RTX 5070 Ti you can still swap out later
highlights.body: The Legion Tower 7i Gen 10 pairs an RTX 5070 Ti and Core Ultra 7 265F with 32GB of DDR5, a 2TB NVMe on the higher trim and a 1200W power supply, and it does that on a standard ATX motherboard with a standard 24-pin connector. The 1200W headroom matters more than the benchmark numbers. It means the next GPU generation drops straight in, and in a year where components cost what they cost, a chassis that accepts a staged upgrade is worth several hundred dollars on its own. The RTX 5080 trim at $2,089 keeps the same logic intact.

highlights.title: Order the base memory and buy your own sticks, every single time
highlights.body: Factory memory upgrades became the highest-margin line item on a 2026 configurator. Going from 16GB to 32GB at checkout runs from about $120 at the value brands to roughly $360 at the premium ones, for identical commodity DDR5 DIMMs that cost the manufacturer the same. Buy the machine at its base memory tier, then add a matched kit yourself. DDR5 is expensive at retail too, and this move still comes out ahead by $80 to $250 depending on the brand. It takes four minutes and one screwdriver.

highlights.title: Cost per frame is the only number that compares brands honestly
highlights.body: Spec sheets flatter machines that stack impressive part names at whatever price the vendor likes. Measured average frame rate divided by the actual transaction price cuts through that immediately. Run it across this list and the ordering falls out on its own: Lenovo at $1,709 with an RTX 5070 Ti sits at the top, Skytech and CyberPowerPC hold the value end at $649 to $799, and the boutique builds at $3,000 and up are buying you assembly craft and support rather than throughput. Decide which of those two things you are actually paying for.

highlights.title: Check the power supply wattage and the motherboard standard before anything else
highlights.body: A prebuilt with a proprietary board layout or a 500W supply is a machine that ends its life the day its GPU does. That has always been true, and in 2026 it costs real money, because staged upgrades are how most people will get through the current component prices. The Omen 35L, the Legion Tower 7i, the iBUYPOWER Y40 Pro, the Corsair Vengeance i7500 and the Maingear MG-1 all use retail ATX internals throughout. Confirm the wattage, the board form factor and the maximum GPU length the chassis accepts, then look at the benchmark charts.

zh-tw.commentary:
老實說，「自己組比較便宜」這句話我講了十五年，今年正式失效了。

2025 年中一組 32GB DDR5-6000 大概兩千五出頭就買得到，現在同一組要一萬三千多，光是七月 DDR5 合約價又漲了 7%，整體比一年前高出 448%。大型整機廠在漲價前用貨櫃單位掃記憶體跟 NAND，成本早就鎖死了，所以 2026 年 8 月的品牌機價格，常常比你照著同樣規格去原價屋開單還便宜。這個比較我這個月自己算過四次，四次都是品牌機贏。

也因為這樣，Valve Steam Machine 在這一題裡是最有參考價值的一台。Valve 直接講明成本價出貨，1,049 美元這個數字等於把 2026 年 6 月的真實零件成本公開標價，換算台幣大約三萬三，效能約是 Steam Deck 的六倍。任何一台比它貴的機器，都得拿出對得起價差的效能。它排在第二，理由很實際：SteamOS 目前約有兩萬五千款遊戲能跑，你手上那幾款很可能剛好在名單外，而且台灣沒有正式通路，要買得靠代購。

第一名我給 Lenovo Legion Tower 7i Gen 10。NT$53,900 買到 RTX 5070 Ti、Core Ultra 7 265F、32GB DDR5、1200W 電源，用幀數去除價格它直接勝出，而且裡面是標準 ATX 主機板配標準 24pin 電源，這台可以再撐兩代顯卡。

最後講一個能幫你省最多錢的習慣，跟你選哪個品牌無關：下單就選最低的記憶體配置，記憶體自己買自己插。原廠 16GB 升 32GB 的加價，各家從三千八到一萬一都有，插的是規格完全一樣的通用 DDR5。

highlights.title: Steam Machine 是全站排序的那把尺
highlights.body: Valve 公開表示 Steam Machine 以成本價販售，512GB 版 1,049 美元、2TB 版 1,349 美元，並說明原本的目標價接近 750 美元，價差全部來自記憶體與 NAND 漲價。這代表它是這個品類裡唯一一台把料件成本誠實攤開的機器。我把它當基準線用：任何一台 Windows 品牌機開價超過台幣三萬三，就得拿出明顯更高的效能來對應那個價差。這一招可以幫你省掉一整個下午的規格表比對，也是為什麼一台要價七萬五、只配 RTX 5070 的機器，在每幀成本這一項會落在現在的位置。

highlights.title: Lenovo 拿第一，是因為五萬三買到的 RTX 5070 Ti 之後還能自己換掉
highlights.body: Legion Tower 7i Gen 10 用 RTX 5070 Ti 配 Core Ultra 7 265F、32GB DDR5，高階配置給到 2TB NVMe，電源直接上 1200W，而且主機板是標準 ATX、電源接頭是標準 24pin。1200W 這個數字比跑分還重要，它的意思是下一代顯卡買回來直接插上去就能動。在零件價格這麼硬的年份，一台能讓你分階段升級的機殼，本身就值好幾千塊。RTX 5080 的配置賣 NT$65,900 左右，同樣的邏輯依然成立。

highlights.title: 記憶體一律選最低配，剩下的自己插
highlights.body: 原廠記憶體升級在 2026 年變成配置頁上毛利最高的一欄。結帳時從 16GB 升到 32GB，平價品牌加價大約三千八，高階品牌可以喊到一萬一，插的是成本完全相同的通用 DDR5 顆粒。正確做法是機器買最低記憶體配置，然後自己去買一組對稱的套條回來插。零售的 DDR5 現在也不便宜，但這樣做仍然能省下兩千五到八千不等，看你買的是哪個品牌。整個過程四分鐘，一支螺絲起子就搞定。

highlights.title: 每幀成本是唯一能誠實橫向比較的數字
highlights.body: 規格表對那種堆滿漂亮料號、價格隨廠商開的機器特別友善。用實測平均幀數去除實際成交價，這層濾鏡馬上就破了。把這條公式套進這份榜單，排序自己就跑出來了：Lenovo 用 NT$53,900 配 RTX 5070 Ti 站上第一，Skytech 跟 CyberPowerPC 以兩萬到兩萬五守住入門段，而九萬以上的精品組裝機，你買的是組裝工藝跟售後服務。先想清楚你花的這筆錢要換哪一樣。

highlights.title: 先看電源瓦數跟主機板規格，再去看跑分
highlights.body: 一台用專屬主機板、配 500W 電源的品牌機，壽命會跟它那張顯卡一起結束。這件事一直都成立，只是在 2026 年它變成真金白銀的損失，因為多數人接下來都得靠分階段升級撐過這波零件行情。Omen 35L、Legion Tower 7i、iBUYPOWER Y40 Pro、Corsair Vengeance i7500 跟 Maingear MG-1 全部走市售 ATX 規格。買之前先確認三件事：電源瓦數、主機板板型、機殼能塞多長的顯卡，確認完再去看跑分圖表。

en.commentary:
The memory market is now the single biggest factor in this category, and I have adjusted for it. A 64GB DDR5-5600 kit that averaged 191 dollars in August 2025 was selling for 1,118 dollars by 17 August 2026, a 485 percent rise in a year, driven by fabs shifting capacity to HBM for AI accelerators. Nvidia has also raised board partner pricing three times this year, most recently by 20 to 30 percent this month.

That is why I have raised the Valve Steam Machine's memory markup score to 9.7 and its overall to 9.1. Its price is locked at 1,049 dollars with memory included, so while DIY builders watch a 32GB kit climb toward 400 dollars, that config risk simply is not yours. A sealed, fixed-price box is a genuinely different proposition in this market than it was a year ago.

The Lenovo Legion Tower 7i Gen 10 keeps first place on a 9.6 cost per frame score and 9.4 on upgrade freedom. In a year when memory is the expensive part, buying a machine that lets you add sticks later at your own timing is worth real money.

My blunt advice for anyone shopping now: buy the memory configuration you actually want on day one where the markup is reasonable, because the aftermarket is the expensive path this year. That reverses the standard advice, and the price data supports it.

highlights.body: Its 1,049 dollar price includes memory and is locked, so the DDR5 spike that is hitting DIY builders does not land on this buyer.

highlights.title: DDR5 is up 485 percent in a year
highlights.body: A 64GB DDR5-5600 kit averaged 191 dollars last August and reached 1,118 dollars by 17 August 2026 as fabs shifted capacity to HBM.

highlights.title: GPU pricing moved again this month
highlights.body: Nvidia raised board partner pricing for the third time this year, by roughly 20 to 30 percent, which flows into prebuilt sticker prices next quarter.

highlights.title: Buy the RAM config you want up front
highlights.body: With aftermarket kits at four to five times last year's price, paying a reasonable factory markup on day one is now the cheaper path.

zh-tw.commentary:

The memory markup factor in this ranking has become the single most important number, and this week's data makes the case cleanly. A 32GB DDR5 kit that cost roughly ninety dollars a year ago now runs three hundred seventy five to four hundred dollars, and TrendForce forecasts conventional DRAM contract prices rising another thirteen to eighteen percent this quarter.

Here is why that matters more for a prebuilt buyer than for someone building their own machine. System integrators buy memory in volume on contracts negotiated months ahead. A builder ordering today pays spot retail. That gap has widened so far that a prebuilt with 32GB now frequently costs less than the sum of its parts bought individually, which reverses the usual arithmetic of this category entirely.

The Lenovo Legion Tower 7i Gen 10 holds first at 9.3 because Lenovo's memory contracts have kept its configurations priced sensibly while retail DDR5 climbed. The HP Omen 35L at 8.8 is my recommendation for buyers who want upgrade freedom, because its standard parts and accessible interior mean you are not locked into proprietary components later.

zh-tw.commentary:
Lenovo Legion Tower 7i Gen 10 依然第一，總分 9.3，而 Steam Machine 剛好是一把很好用的尺。報導指出 Valve 入門款起價 1,049 美元，搭六核心 AMD Zen 4 處理器與 8GB 顯示記憶體。這個價位框出了整個品類的基準，Windows Central 也主張，幾款搭獨立 RTX 50 系列顯卡的品牌桌機，在同價位的效能表現更強。

Legion 的實力在每格效能成本 9.6 與升級自由度 9.4。機殼打開就能換顯卡、加硬碟，幾年後還能升級，塔式主機的價值就在這裡回收。Steam Machine 仍以 9.1 穩居第二，每格效能成本 9.8、記憶體加價 9.7，開箱即用的划算程度很漂亮，升級自由度 6.2 則說明了它的天花板在哪。

HP Omen 35L 第三 8.8，升級自由度 9.2。如果我打算用五年，又希望有熟悉的保固通路，會選它。

如果你是預算有限的學生或剛出社會的上班族，我建議先決定要不要升級，再決定買哪一台，這樣花的錢才會落在真正有感的地方。

TechPowerUp 報導顯卡價格一個月內上漲 15%，所以下單前我會再確認一次當下的配置與價格。這週排名維持不動。
